notes.craft: Saint James knits and sews in its own workshops in Saint-James, Normandy (75 looms, 100+ seamstresses, per its know-how page), and its Breton, knit and peacoat pages say they are made there. But half the sampled product pages (a polyester bomber, a canvas jacket, a tee) give no origin, and a separate Made-in-France collection suggests not everything is French-made. A strong 4, a 5 if the unlabelled lines prove to be in-house.

cities: No store of its own in the US · department stores and independent menswear shops, and its own site

marks: A HOUSE technical material with its own coined name: UVYL. Declared verbatim on the brand's own fabric guide - 'Anti-UV UVYL. What is UVYL? craft_evidence.owned_d: Brand's own workshops in the town of Saint-James, Normandy. Know-how page: 'one of the largest knitting workshops in Europe, with no less than 75 knitting looms'; 'more than 100 seamstresses work in the clothing workshop'; in-house mending (raccoutreuses). History page: offices and workshops have stayed in the region since 1889; 300+ employees; bought by its employees in 1990. Spinning and dyeing not described as in-house today. Covers knitwear, Breton tops and at least some tailoring (peacoat 'crafted in our Ateliers in Normandy'); some sampled items give no origin.
craft_evidence.countries: France 3/6 product-specific (Breton shirt, cardigan, peacoat); 3/6 no product-specific origin (ST DARIO polyester bomber, Zephyr cotton jacket, Arsene tee), only the site-wide 'Made in France' banner.
